title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Jane Street and NVIDIA engineers show how to implement the three Mamba-2 forward-pass kernels in the Python-based CUDA Tile (cuTile) DSL, and report 1.14x to 1.82x kernel-level speedups over an open-source Triton implementation on a Blackwell Ultra B300. The post doubles as a showcase for cuTile and a quant trading firm's adoption of it.

insights.claim: CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python DSL and tile-centric programming model that hides thread- and warp-level scheduling so the compiler automatically targets Tensor Cores and other advanced GPU features.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is pushing a higher-level, Python-first kernel authoring path that competes with Triton for developer mindshare.
insights.quote: By abstracting thread- and warp-level scheduling behind high-level, tile-centric primitives, cuTile enables you to write GPU kernels in Python

insights.claim: Jane Street, described as a deeply technical global trading firm using deep learning for quantitative research, is an early adopter that implemented Mamba-2 in cuTile and partnered with NVIDIA to optimise the kernels.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: A sophisticated quant shop validating cuTile is useful reference-customer evidence for NVIDIA's software moat.
insights.quote: As an early adopter of cuTile, machine learning engineers at Jane Street implemented Mamba-2

themes.theme: Why Mamba-2 and how it maps to GPUs

insights.claim: Softmax attention trains fast on Tensor Cores but its inference compute and memory grow linearly with sequence length, while RNNs have constant inference cost but slow, nonparallelizable training; Mamba-2 aims for the best of both.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Sequence-model architecture choice is a tradeoff between training parallelism and inference cost, which state-space models try to dissolve.
insights.quote: Sequence modeling architectures face a computational trade-off

insights.claim: Mamba-2 keeps a fixed-size hidden state that is a matrix rather than an RNN vector, giving more representational capacity, with a recurrent update that can be computed chunkwise using Tensor Cores.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: The matrix state is what lets chunked matmul formulations exploit Tensor Cores.
insights.quote: Similar to an RNN, it has a fixed size hidden state and a recurrent update that can be computed chunkwise

insights.claim: A parallel-scan approach to training and prefill would materialise an enormous hidden-state tensor, making it memory-bound and unable to use Tensor Cores, so the chunked matrix-multiplication 'jump formula' is used instead.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Algorithm reformulation, not just kernel tuning, is what unlocks hardware utilisation for state-space models.
insights.quote: this approach requires materializing an enormous hidden state tensor making it primarily memory-bound and unable to utilize Tensor Cores

insights.claim: Without the decay term, Mamba-2 reduces to linear attention (without softmax) with some renaming, which is why its chunk computation looks like causal attention with a mask.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Close kinship with linear attention means kernel techniques can transfer across these architectures.
insights.quote: when the decay term is removed, Mamba-2 is just linear attention (with some renaming)

insights.claim: Because all decay values are negative, every kept exponential in the masked computation has a non-positive argument, which guarantees numerical stability; positive-argument exponentials are masked out before they can overflow.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Numerical safety is built into the formulation, allowing low-precision Tensor Core use.
insights.quote: Any exponentials of positive numbers are never kept, guaranteeing numerical stability.

insights.claim: The forward pass is split into three kernels: chunk_cumsum for intra-chunk cumulative decay in log-space, fwd_pass_state for chunk-initial hidden states, and compute_out for outputs, with exp2 scaled by log2(e) used instead of exp for speed.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: A reusable decomposition for implementing state-space layers on tile-based GPU languages.
insights.quote: Since it’s much cheaper to compute exp2 instead of exp, the result is scaled by log2(e).

insights.claim: compute_out fuses the carried-state term, decayed causal interaction matrix and skip connection into one tiled kernel, keeping the C-times-B-transpose matrix in registers instead of materialising a full [B, n_chunks, chunk_size, chunk_size] tensor in global memory.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Fusion that avoids global-memory round trips is the main source of speedup versus a naive PyTorch version.
insights.quote: compute_out fuses them into one tiled kernel and keeps that matrix in registers.

insights.claim: On Blackwell's fifth-generation Tensor Core, operand A can live in Tensor Memory while operand B must be in Shared Memory, so the authors use the B^T A^T = (AB)^T identity to route the fused operand to A and relieve shared-memory contention.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Blackwell-specific operand placement shows kernel authors must tune for new memory hierarchies.
insights.quote: operand A can live in Tensor Memory, but operand B must live in Shared Memory

insights.claim: Transposing decay_cumsum and dt to a [batch, head, token] layout makes memory access contiguous and enables TMA, avoiding cache-unfriendly strided LDG instructions.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Memory layout changes are a major lever on achieved bandwidth.
insights.quote: The default strided memory access for decay_cumsum and dt lowers to cache-unfriendly LDG instructions.

insights.claim: Since bottlenecks shift with input shape, the authors use an autotuner over block size, occupancy and the other optimisation choices through cuTile's exhaustive_search to find the best configuration per shape.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Per-shape autotuning is becoming standard in high-performance kernel stacks.
insights.quote: no single optimization strategy fits every model configuration

insights.claim: On a single NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (Blackwell Ultra) the optimised cuTile Mamba-2 forward kernels were 1.14x to 1.82x faster than the open-source Triton mamba_ssm kernel, with gains growing at longer sequences and larger state sizes.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Vendor-run result on NVIDIA's newest hardware favouring NVIDIA's own DSL; useful but not independent.
insights.quote: the optimized cuTile forward-pass kernels are 1.14x to 1.82x faster

insights.claim: The speedups are kernel-level only, and end-to-end training outcomes will also depend on the backward pass, which a follow-up post will cover.
insights.speaker: Sylvain Gugger
insights.so_what: Headline gains may not translate fully to training throughput until the backward pass is optimised.
insights.quote: Note that these are kernel-level speedups only and end-to-end training results will also depend on the backward pass implementations.
